fields.name: Listing Image URLs
fields.description: Newline-separated source image URLs captured at intake (web scrape, portal listing, agency site). Written by the NPC Email 1 Make scenario. These are candidates, not storage: the dashboard's listing-images function copies the bytes into its own bucket and renders from there, because portal hotlinks rot and Airtable attachment URLs expire within hours. Keep newest-first - the first URL is treated as the hero shot.

fields.name: Images Captured At
fields.description: When this record's image set was last captured or refreshed by intake. This is the freshness signal the Listings page sorts and labels on - it answers "how recent are these photos", which Created Time cannot, because a record created in January can have its photos re-scraped in August. Set it whenever Listing Images or Listing Image URLs is written; leave it alone when nothing about the images changed.

fields.name: Primary Image URL
fields.description: The hero shot - the first entry of Listing Image URLs, lifted into its own column so a card, an interface gallery or a report cover can read one value instead of parsing a newline list.

fields.name: Image Count
fields.description: How many image candidates intake captured for this record. Zero is meaningful: it separates "we looked and there were no photos" from "we never looked", which Listing Image URLs being empty cannot express on its own.

fields.name: Image Source
fields.description: Where the image candidates came from. Ranked in the dashboard: an agent's own photos outrank a scrape, and Street View is a picture of a location rather than of the property, so it only ever leads when nothing else exists.

fields.name: Intake Content Hash
fields.description: Stable fingerprint of the listing's identifying content (normalised address + suburb + postcode, or project + stage when there is no street address). Intake writes it so duplicate detection can match on one exact value instead of a LIKE against a free-text address - the old approach, which broke on apostrophes and on the same property arriving with "St" one week and "Street" the next.

fields.name: Entity Classification
fields.description: Map from payload field `entityClassification`. From form version stage-1-priority-access-v3 the option set is: buyers_agent, property_advisory, real_estate_agency, mortgage_finance, developer, construction, accounting_smsf, conveyancing_legal, property_management, multi_service_group, technology_partner, other. Retired slugs (wealth_advisor, financial_planner, investment_group, enterprise, enterprise_property_network) are historical only. Readable equivalents are available in payload field `organisationTypeLabel`.

fields.name: Annual Transactional Value
fields.description: Map from payload field `annualOriginationTransactionVolume`. From form version stage-1-priority-access-v3 the incoming values are CLIENT/TRANSACTION COUNTS, not dollar brackets: pre_launch_under_10, 10_to_25, 26_to_75, 76_to_150, 151_to_300, 301_to_500, over_500, not_yet_known. The older dollar-bracket choices are historical. Readable equivalents are available in payload field `annualVolumeLabel`.

fields.name: Current Bottlenecks
fields.description: Applicant's own description of current technology/workflow bottlenecks. Required, max 1000 characters. Map from payload field `currentTechStackBottlenecks`. From form version stage-1-priority-access-v3 this carries the applicant's text only — the structured priorities now live in "Primary Areas to Improve".

fields.name: Phone
fields.description: Map from payload field `mobileNumber`. Required from form version stage-1-priority-access-v3 and normalised to E.164 (+61… for Australian numbers, explicit country code otherwise).

fields.name: Your Role
fields.description: Stage 1 waitlist form. Map from payload field `roleLabel` (human-readable). The slug equivalent is `role`.

fields.name: Primary Areas to Improve
fields.description: Stage 1 waitlist form, maximum three selections. Map from payload field `primaryAreasToImproveLabels` (array). The slug equivalent is `primaryAreasToImprove`.

choices.name: Disconnected systems and duplicate data entry

fields.name: Additional Notes
fields.description: Stage 1 waitlist form, optional free text, max 500 characters. Map from payload field `additionalNotes`. Applicant-supplied — keep separate from the internal Notes field.

fields.name: Application ID
fields.description: Non-sequential public application reference generated by the form (AX-XXXXXXXXXX). Map from payload field `applicationId`. Also sent as the X-Application-Id header — use it as the deduplication key.

fields.name: Form Version
fields.description: Schema version of the waitlist form that produced the record, currently stage-1-priority-access-v3. Map from payload field `formVersion`.

fields.name: Privacy Acknowledged
fields.description: Required collection-notice acknowledgement, ticked by the applicant at submission. Map from payload field `privacyAcknowledged`.

fields.name: Marketing Consent
fields.description: Optional, separate consent to product, event and future-intake updates. Unticked by default — do not send marketing unless this is true. Map from payload field `marketingConsent`.

fields.name: Privacy Notice Version
fields.description: Version of the collection notice shown at submission, currently collection-notice-2026-07-v1. Map from payload field `privacyNoticeVersion`.

fields.name: Source
fields.description: Submission source recorded by the form, e.g. AURIXA Contact Waitlist Page. Map from payload field `source`.

fields.name: Landing Page
fields.description: First page of the visitor's session including query string, captured silently. Map from payload field `landingPage`.

fields.name: Referrer
fields.description: Referring URL for the visitor's session, blank on direct visits. Map from payload field `referrer`.

fields.name: UTM Source

fields.name: UTM Medium

fields.name: UTM Campaign
fields.description: Campaign utm_campaign captured from the landing URL. Map from payload field `utmCampaign`.

fields.name: UTM Term

fields.name: UTM Content
fields.description: Campaign utm_content captured from the landing URL. Map from payload field `utmContent`.

fields.name: Application ID Key
fields.description: Normalised Application ID (upper case, trimmed). Match on this rather than the raw field so a reference the applicant typed by hand — the fallback when their secure link has expired — still resolves regardless of case or stray spaces.

fields.name: Stage 2 Response Count
fields.description: How many Business Readiness Responses are linked to this applicant. Non-zero means the applicant reached Stage 2.

fields.name: Stage 2 Detailed Count
fields.description: How many BRQ Detailed Responses are linked to this applicant. Counted separately because the questionnaire writes the detailed table first.

fields.name: Stage 2 Completion Status
fields.description: Completion Status pulled through from the linked Business Readiness Responses (Draft / Submitted / Reviewed).

fields.name: Stage 2 Started At
fields.description: Earliest Submitted At across the linked BRQ Detailed Responses — the moment this applicant actually moved to Stage 2 on the front end.

fields.name: Stage 2 Reached
fields.description: 1 when a Stage 2 response of either kind is linked to this applicant. This is the progression signal the Stage 1 reminder must respect — it only becomes 1 once a response is actually linked, so an unlinked response will not suppress the email.

fields.name: Token Expires At
fields.description: Expiry of the secure Stage 2 link, read straight out of the `expires` parameter on Bypass URL (URL-decoded). Derived rather than stored so it can never drift from the link that was actually emailed. If the link format ever changes, replace this formula with a written dateTime field.

fields.name: Token Status
fields.description: Live state of the emailed Stage 2 link. Once this reads Expired the applicant can no longer use the link and must enter their Application ID instead — which is why the reference is shown to them at Stage 1 and stored here.

fields.name: Stage 2 Invite Sent At
fields.description: When the Stage 1 reminder inviting the applicant into Stage 2 was last sent. Written by the "Aurixa Waitlist Stage 1" Make scenario in the same module that stores Email Message ID.

fields.name: Stage 2 Invite Count
fields.description: How many Stage 2 invitations have gone to this applicant. Increment it when the reminder sends, so a repeating schedule can be capped without a second source of truth.

fields.name: Send Stage 2 Invite
fields.description: THE GATE. Reads SEND or HOLD. Filter the Stage 1 reminder on this field (text equals SEND) between the "Get a record" and "Create a message" modules, so the value is re-read after the delay and an applicant who has since completed Stage 2 is skipped. See Stage 2 Invite Hold Reason for why a record is held.

fields.name: Stage 2 Invite Hold Reason
fields.description: Plain-English reason the gate reads HOLD, so a suppressed reminder is explainable without opening the scenario history.

fields.name: Stage 3 Booking Count
fields.description: How many Strategic Review Bookings are linked to this applicant. Non-zero means the applicant reached Stage 3.

fields.name: Stage 3 Booked At
fields.description: Earliest Submitted At across the linked Strategic Review Bookings — the moment this applicant actually moved to Stage 3 on the front end.

fields.name: Stage 3 Session Start
fields.description: Latest requested session start across the linked bookings — the time that currently stands, so a reschedule supersedes the original.

fields.name: Stage 3 Booking Status
fields.description: Booking Status pulled through from the linked Strategic Review Bookings (Requested / Confirmed / Rescheduled / Cancelled / Completed / No Show).

fields.name: Stage 3 Active Bookings
fields.description: How many linked bookings still stand — cancellations and no-shows are excluded. This, not the raw count, is what the Stage 3 gate reads.

fields.name: Stage 3 Reached
fields.description: 1 when a booking that still stands is linked to this applicant. This is the progression signal the Stage 3 reminder must respect — it only becomes 1 once a booking is actually linked, so an unlinked booking will not suppress the email, and it falls back to 0 if the session is cancelled.

fields.name: Stage 3 Booking URL
fields.description: The Stage 3 equivalent of Bypass URL, and deliberately not a token link: the scheduler is reached with the Application ID itself, so there is nothing to expire and nothing to reissue. Built from Application ID Key so it is always the normalised reference. This is the link the Stage 2 completion email and any Stage 3 reminder should use.

fields.name: Stage 3 Invite Sent At
fields.description: When the reminder inviting the applicant to book their strategic review was last sent. Mirrors Stage 2 Invite Sent At.

fields.name: Stage 3 Invite Count
fields.description: How many invitations to book a strategic review have gone to this applicant. Increment it when the reminder sends, so a repeating schedule can be capped without a second source of truth.

fields.name: Send Stage 3 Invite
fields.description: THE GATE, Stage 3. Reads SEND or HOLD. Filter the "book your strategic review" reminder on this field (text equals SEND) between the "Get a record" and "Create a message" modules, so the value is re-read after the delay and an applicant who has since booked is skipped. It is deliberately the mirror of Send Stage 2 Invite, with two differences: it also holds until the applicant has actually reached Stage 2 (before that, the Stage 2 invite is the one that should be going out), and it caps at three invitations. See Stage 3 Invite Hold Reason for why a record is held.

fields.name: Stage 3 Invite Hold Reason
fields.description: Plain-English reason the Stage 3 gate reads HOLD, so a suppressed reminder is explainable without opening the scenario history. Blank when the gate reads SEND.

config.formula:
IF(
  {fldtNFwOfeTaaELKI} = 1,
  "Applicant already booked a strategic review",
  IF(
    {fldrn1evbYmFjoPyA} != 1,
    "Applicant has not reached Stage 2 yet",
    IF(
      {fldFAjPdUqraeUCoP} = "Declined",
      "Application declined",
      IF(
        {fldU6Ny4Ck482jpGg} = BLANK(),
        "No Application ID on the record",
        IF(
          {fldvcq6GjkuBTREON} = BLANK(),
          "No corporate email to send to",
          IF({fldJyjTTa8kzfA2lD} >= 3, "Invitation limit reached", "")
        )
      )
    )
  )
)

fields.name: Stage 3 Access (Application)
fields.description:
HALF OF THE ADMISSION POLICY for the Stage 3 scheduling page: the half that is a property of THIS record. Reads GRANT or DENY, and denies an application with no Application ID or one that has been declined.

The other half — the applicant must have completed Stage 2 — is deliberately NOT here. It is checked by the "Aurixa Stage 3 Access" scenario directly against BRQ Detailed Responses, by Application ID. That row is written by the Stage 2 scenario at the moment the questionnaire is submitted, so admission depends on nothing asynchronous. Reading Stage 2 Reached instead would have made page access depend on the "Link Stage 2 detailed response to applicant" automation having already run — and on nobody ever switching it off — which is not a safe thing for a gate to rest on.

Both halves must pass. A reference that fails either is answered identically, so the page can never reveal whether a particular application exists.

fields.name: Stage 3 Access Denied Reason (Application)
fields.description:
Plain-English reason this record fails the application half of the Stage 3 admission policy. Blank when that half passes — which does not by itself mean the applicant can book, because Stage 3 also requires a Stage 2 response, checked against BRQ Detailed Responses rather than against this table. For that half, Stage 2 Detailed Count is the field to look at.

Never sent to the browser: the website is told only that it could not verify the reference.

config.formula:
IF(
  {fldU6Ny4Ck482jpGg} = BLANK(),
  "No Application ID on the record",
  IF({fldFAjPdUqraeUCoP} = "Declined", "Application declined", "")
)

fields.name: Booking Reference

fields.name: Send Booking Confirmation
fields.description: THE GATE. Reads SEND or HOLD. Filter the Stage 3 confirmation on this field (text equals SEND) between the "Get a record" and "Create a message" modules, so it is re-read after the delay and a booking that was cancelled, or already confirmed, is skipped. Holding on Confirmation Message ID is what makes a re-run of the scenario safe: the second pass sees the id written by the first and sends nothing. See Booking Confirmation Hold Reason for why a record is held.

fields.name: Booking Confirmation Hold Reason
fields.description: Plain-English reason the gate reads HOLD, so a suppressed confirmation is explainable without opening the scenario history. Blank when the gate reads SEND.

fields.name: Counts As Booked
fields.description: 1 when this booking should count as the applicant having reached Stage 3. Cancellations and no-shows read 0 so the Stage 3 reminder starts going out again — summing this on Aurixa Waitlist is what makes the gate self-correcting.
